A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ViT feature-distillation work and retain the same two student modifications and classification experiments. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and support comparison despite substantial rewriting and reformatting.

before.justification: v1 reports original ImageNet-1K distillation, ablation, and standalone-training results in Tables 2–7, plus original SVD and SEP analyses in the main text and Appendices A–B.

after.justification: v2 retains those original classification results and reports additional shared-subspace PCA and cross-model representation analyses in Table 1, Figure 1, and Appendices B–C.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains the inference-retained linear projector and final-block widening, with the same combined classification, logit-distillation, and feature-loss objective. Strategy 1/2 are renamed Lift/WideLast. The new PCA diagnostic changes their rationale; omission of the explicit normalized-MSE formula does not establish a different implementation.

E1.justification: Both versions use ImageNet-1K for classification and ImageNet validation images for representation analysis. The additional DINO, DINOv2, MAE, and CLIP encoders are model configurations analyzed on the retained image data, not new evaluated datasets, multimodal tasks, or input domains.

E2.justification: Comparator membership in Tables 2–7 is unchanged: the same standalone baselines, SoftKD, MSE, SpectralKD, and listed combinations remain in corresponding experiments. Newly discussed methods such as OFA-KD and RSD are related work, not additional evaluated KD comparators.

E3.justification: v2 introduces a substantially different diagnostic protocol: pooling token features from 1,000 images to estimate an uncentered shared PCA basis and evaluating reconstruction under that fixed basis alongside per-image SVD. Representation-analysis configurations expand from six to fourteen models. The classification experiments retain their stated dataset, training budget, and accuracy metric.

E4.justification: The new SVD-versus-PCA analyses test whether per-image compressibility implies a compact shared subspace, while expanded cross-model diagnostics examine this behavior across pretraining regimes. These substantially revise the mechanistic evidence. v1's layer-wise and stage-wise rank profiles are removed; the classifier-head, projector-width, and loss-weight ablations remain unchanged.

E5.justification: v1 explicitly states that ViT-Huge (MAE) was checked on two random 1,000-image subsets; v2 omits this repeated-subset information. This is a reporting removal, not evidence that fewer checks were performed. Across-image SEP standard-deviation bands remain, and neither version reports repeated-training-run uncertainty for classification accuracies.

E6.justification: New results include CaiT-S24 shared-PCA dimensions of 302 and 359 at 95% and 99% energy for approximately 99% of images, alongside retained per-image SVD values of 61 and 121. Tables 1 and 8 add model results and spectral summaries, while depth-profile results disappear. All classification values in Tables 2–7 and overlapping endpoint SVD/SEP values are unchanged.

T1.justification: v2 corrects v1's inference that per-image SVD rank percentiles guarantee one shared low-dimensional projector. Sections 2.1–2.2 distinguish input-dependent factorizations from a fixed shared basis, acknowledge the token-count rank ceiling, and introduce channel second-moment and shared reconstruction-energy definitions. This changes foundational mathematical reasoning, not merely notation.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion replace the globally low-rank teacher premise with per-image low rank and substantial dataset-level subspace rotation. The claimed failure regime is narrowed to wide-to-narrow ViT compression, acknowledging successful representation transfer between comparable models. The two remedies and headline accuracy claims remain.

C2.justification: v1 explains failure through insufficient token bandwidth within a purported shared low-rank space. v2 interprets encoding mismatch as both orientation and bandwidth mismatch, explicitly acknowledging that fixed Lift cannot resolve subspace rotation and attributing input-dependent alignment capacity to WideLast. This materially changes the mechanism explanation and qualifies what each remedy addresses.

D1.justification: v2 documents the uncentered PCA computation and newly states that code and raw data accompany supplementary materials, whose availability cannot be verified from the PDFs. It omits v1's explicit LayerNorm-normalized MSE and detached-teacher specifications, minimum learning rate, cooldown, and logit-loss weight. These are documentation changes, not established implementation changes.

R1.justification: The new five-part related-work appendix substantially positions the work against low-rank compression, explicit alignment, selective distillation, and teacher conditioning. Added discussions include GhostNet, Yu and Wu, OFA-KD, and RSD; the introduction also distinguishes CLIP representation transfer from compression. Numerous generic KD and language-model references are removed.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, representation analysis, contribution list, and conclusion undergo substantial rewriting around per-image versus shared geometry. Terminology becomes Lift/WideLast, a dedicated related-work appendix is introduced, and the diagnostic appendices are reorganized. Author-list and citation-style changes accompany this broader narrative revision.

P2.justification: The main text changes from single-column to two-column layout. Figure 1 and the SVD appendix displays are redesigned around PCA spectra, shared reconstruction curves, and overlaid SVD/PCA histograms. Tables 1 and 8 gain substantial column and row structure; SEP displays expand to additional models while the original six-model panels are retained and rearranged.

improvement.justification: v2 resolves a central weakness: v1 incorrectly inferred a shared compact projector from per-image SVD ranks. Sections 2.1–2.2 correct that reasoning, and new PCA evidence directly demonstrates the distinction, including 302 shared-PCA dimensions versus 61 per-image SVD dimensions for CaiT-S24 at 95% energy for approximately 99% of images. Cross-model diagnostics and narrower compression claims substantially strengthen the scientific argument. Some loss and training details are omitted, weakening reproducibility, but this limited loss is outweighed by the foundational correction and supporting evidence.
